correctness.rationale: Re-audited repairs/5/RESULT.md and its verification notes. Kernel normalization gives the principal power; Schwarz–Pick for φ(w)/w gives a uniform modulus gap from one off any small disk, including near |w|=1. For t=|w|² the first angular perturbation is −s e^(−iϑ)b t^ν e^(imθ) in rotated coordinates. Analyticity in √t gives a uniform radial derivative, with real leading constant s|1−a|>0. At fixed depth x each angle gives a unique local t=t_a(x)+O(x^ν); its change in the imaginary linear-symbol curve is O(x^(ν+1)) because that curve has real tangent in these coordinates. The circle is connected and the harmonic attains both extrema, so the exact local section is an interval and the coefficient is s|b|(s|1−a|)^(−ν). For d=1−a, the t² coefficient of the rotated linear-model curve is s|d|[a−(s−1)d/2]; composing its imaginary part with t_a(x)=x/(s|d|)+O(x²) gives h(x)=(s+1) Im(a) x²/(2s|d|)+O(x³). This also verifies the dominance of the centerline when m≥3 and a is nonreal. The half-width determines the exponent and, for known a,s, |b|. Boundedness is assumed, not inferred from being a disk self-map. The original proof also supports its convexity conclusion, but that conclusion is omitted from the repaired finding on originality grounds. The frozen checker was read, not run; its recorded finite samples are not the proof.
